sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A02
A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint stop-and-yield; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F05 and sec09-F07.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
Yellow warns of hazards on a diamond, while orange warns of road work on a diamond or rectangle [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F03 and sec09-F21.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A03
A do not pass sign is a rectangle marking the no-passing stretch itself, while the no passing zone pennant on the left merely points to where that stretch begins [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint passing-signs; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec09-F11 and sec09-F12.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A03
A reduced speed ahead sign only tells you to start slowing, while the speed limit sign after it is where the lower limit actually takes effect [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint speed-signs; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec09-F09 and sec09-F08.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A04
A pass with care sign ends a no-passing zone, while a do not pass sign begins one [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint passing-signs; prereq_hint sec09-R03; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F13 and sec09-F11.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A01
Black and white signs command an action and are always rectangular, while red signs prohibit an action and come in various shapes [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint colors; prereq_hint sec09-R02; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F04 and sec09-F02.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A04
An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to prohibit a movement or activity, while other regulatory signs use black or red lettering on white to state restrictions in words [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint regulatory-signs; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec09-F15 and sec09-F16.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A06
Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right, while stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint work-zones; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec09-F25 and sec09-F24.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A07
A flashing arrow panel steers drivers into a lane or announces a closure, while a flagperson with a flag or paddle stops, slows or guides traffic in person [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint work-zones; prereq_hint sec09-R08; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F26 and sec09-F27.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A02
At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint stop-and-yield; prereq_hint sec09-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec09-F06 and sec09-F05.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A05
Guide and information signs in green, blue or brown locate places and services, while warning signs in yellow describe hazards [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint sign-categories; prereq_hint sec09-R02; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec09-F20 and sec09-F18.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0048]
